qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of results/polish.json and results/editor.json re-computed and matching)
evidence:
All 54 criteria (1 render gate, 2 constraints gate, 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual) were read in full. Most state one conjunctive bar and a matching 'Fails if' list; tolerances such as 'with or without its line break', 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure', 'whichever of Alt+Click and Ctrl/Cmd+Click adds a caret ... scored elsewhere' and the void-attempt rules in cw_stop_cancels_pending_work / cw_newer_run_supersedes are single well-defined bars, and whole-flow bundling is a known false positive that I do not report. Two instances leave the judge two targets.

INSTANCE 1 (enumerate, then waive) - tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:371, cw_history_restore_retry. The body requires: 'Then send that same already completed restore request a second time ... After the second request no fifth revision may exist.' and the closing list repeats 'Fails ... if the repeated request adds a revision'. The same description then waives it: 'If the restore was not sent as a request you can record and replay and the app offers no retry control, say so and leave this one step out without failing the criterion for it.' The public brief makes the behaviour mandatory (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:13: 'If the same restore request is sent again after it was already committed, for example after a lost reply, it must not ...'). So the criterion has two full-credit bars: with the idempotence leg and without it, selected by a judge-side determination ('a request you can record and replay' with 'its method, path, headers and body') that the app cannot be held to and that depends on what the Playwright MCP network listing exposes to the judge. Only this criterion grades repeated-restore idempotence, so when the waiver is taken the requirement is graded nowhere.

INSTANCE 2 (body and closing fail list disagree) - tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:50, cw_undo_redo_availability. Body: 'Type a character: Undo becomes available and Redo stays unavailable. Use Undo: Redo becomes available and Undo is unavailable again.' Closing list: 'Fails if either control looks available straight after New or straight after opening the saved snippet, if either looks available when it has nothing to do at the two later points, or if the app has no visible Undo and Redo controls.' Every listed failure is 'looks available when it should not' or 'no controls'; none covers a control that never becomes available. tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:12 tells the judge 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold, and each ends with the conditions under which it fails', which presents the closing list as the failure conditions, so the positive half of the body and the fail list are two different targets. This is also the negative-without-positive pattern in qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md ('A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing').

Lesser instances of the same body/fail-list gap, reported for completeness and not blocking on their own: cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line (functional judge.toml:245) states a handled-rejection working control ('the marker must appear and the run must finish without an error') that its fail list omits, unlike sibling criteria which end with 'or if the control ... did not'; cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (judge.toml:101) requires the suffix 'exactly once at each caret and nowhere else' while its fail list only names 'fewer than three carets receive the text'; cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion (judge.toml:47) requires Backspace to 'remove only the whole emoji' while its fail list only names leaving half behind. Noted, not counted as a defect: cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus (polish judge.toml:23) enumerates nine controls and then scopes to 'Each of these controls that the app offers and that is enabled at that moment'; that is one conditional bar, though it becomes nearly vacuous for an app offering few of them.

Runtime evidence: the scripted golden results on these bytes (hashes verified for results/polish.json d65b6cf7... and results/editor.json 0e98f453...) exercise the golden only, which has a 'Retry same restore' control (solution/app/src/app.tsx:163) and working Undo/Redo availability, so neither ambiguous branch is exercised. The hosted judge run is on an earlier candidate. No configured judge run exists for these bytes, so how the judge resolves either ambiguity is unmeasured.
counterexample: Instance 1: a submission whose restore is not idempotent (a re-sent committed restore appends another revision, violating behaviour.md:13) and that offers no retry control. A judge that cannot capture the request headers and body from its network listing, or an app that sends restore over a WebSocket, reports the step as not replayable and the criterion still passes on the remaining legs; the same app fails when the judge does manage the replay. Same app, two verdicts, both permitted by the text. Instance 2: a submission whose visible Undo and Redo buttons are rendered permanently disabled (keyboard Undo works). After New and after opening the saved snippet both look unavailable; at the two later points neither 'looks available when it has nothing to do'; visible controls exist. No listed fail condition is met, so a judge following the closing list passes it, while a judge following the body ('Undo becomes available', 'Redo becomes available') fails it.
suggested_fix: cw_undo_redo_availability: add to the fail list 'if Undo is not shown as available after the typed character, or Redo is not shown as available after the Undo'. cw_history_restore_retry: remove the waiver so the bar is single (if no second identical restore request can be sent by a retry control or by replay, the idempotence leg is not shown and the criterion fails), or move repeated-restore idempotence into its own criterion with one stated bar and drop that leg and its fail clause from this one. Optionally add the missing control/positive clauses to the three lesser fail lists.
